Use an asymmetric, two-component model (systolic and diastolic waves) using split-Gaussians to independently control rise and fall times. Set the systolic left width ($\sigma$) to ~31 ms to achieve the target 52 ms rise time. Set the systolic right width to ~120 ms and the diastolic delay to ~300 ms to achieve the target 238 ms pulse width.

This ensures physiological stroke volume variation while reducing the excessive amplitude range.
4.  **Concatenation:** Add the individual pulses onto a continuous time array. This naturally simulates the truncation of diastolic tails and "swallowed" dicrotic notches during rapid sequences, which is a hallmark of AFib in the PPG domain.
